title: Goal factory
description: factory.yaml defines a factory: its runtime, the knowledge sources it uses, skills, agents, board and learning loop. Beside it, environments/<name>.yaml (environment.schema.json) says what each agent's box installs and reaches; every factory has environments/default.yaml (ADR 0037).

id.description: Immutable UUID. Keys the database rows and bucket prefixes, so the name and folder can change freely.

name.description: Human-friendly slug shown in the UI and CLI. Safe to rename.

purpose.description: What the factory is for, in one or two sentences. Agents read it before every item.

description.description: Deprecated alias of purpose, read when purpose is absent.

connections.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): what agents reach is in environments/<name>.yaml. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

sources.description: The organization's knowledge sources the factory's runs read (ADR 0038 decision 5), at most 10 (knowledge-too-many), each listed once (knowledge-source-duplicate). An entry is a source's name, or an object that also says which runs read it (appliesTo) and when (readWhen).

secrets.description: Removed in phase 4 (field-removed): connections hold credentials. Accepted so versions published before still load; goald does not run them.

rules.description: Factory rules (ADR 0014): always-on guidance for the agents each rule's appliesTo targets. Each is a markdown file under rules/ with frontmatter (description, appliesTo, paths).

contracts.description: Named JSON Schemas that station outputs must satisfy. An output contract becomes the model's tool input_schema, so its top level must be "type": "object" with no oneOf, anyOf or allOf there (nested under a property is fine).

starter.description: What a new factory made from this definition starts with (ADR 0032). Onboarding submits starter.item once, when the factory has no items yet.

item.description: A small, safe first item the person watches go through the line.

type.description: One of board.workTypes; when absent, the item gets the first work type, as submitItem does.

oneOf.description: The source's name: every run of the factory reads it.

appliesTo.description: The runs that read the source: ADR 0014's rule scope, matched as a rule's appliesTo is. A run matches when every key set names its agent, station, lane or work type. Without appliesTo, every run reads it.

readWhen.description: One line that replaces the source's own read-when line in this factory's prompt: when its runs should open it.

secretRef.description: A {{secret}} reference: the name of an organization secret open to the factory, in double braces. Valid only in runtime.repository.token, a runtime.repositories entry's token, runtime.modelKey and a trigger's modelAgrees.key, and in environment files.

modelKey.description: The {{secret}} that gives every run its model: a Claude subscription token (sk-ant-oat…) or an Anthropic API key. Jonah's reviews and the tries of past items use it too.

modelConnection.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): set modelKey. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

size.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): set size in each environment file. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

tools.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): set tools in each environment file. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

repository.description: The shorthand for one runtime.repositories entry that writes and is the default, named after the URL's last segment (repo when that is not a slug). It is cloned into each run's box before the agent starts, on the item's branch (goal/<number>-<slug>).

token.description: The {{secret}} that clones, pushes, and reads and merges pull requests. Omit it for a public repository. It reaches the agent's environment only when an environment file names it.

forge.description: The code host the URL is on. github.com is github and gitlab.com is gitlab; any other host needs forge.

connection.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): set token. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

repositories.description: The repositories the factory's runs may open, each with its access. Empty or omitted is a factory with no code. runtime.repository is the shorthand for one entry that writes; a definition has one form or the other.

runner.description: Removed in phase 4 (field-removed): the platform chooses the sandbox backend.

image.description: Removed in phase 4 (field-removed): set image in an environment file.

weeklyUsd.description: Spend cap over a rolling 7 days.

onExhausted.description: At the weekly cap: drain starts no new agent work and lets running tasks finish; stop also stops them. Default drain.

knowledgeBase.description: Removed in phase 4 (field-removed): set knowledge.sources. Accepted so versions published before still load; goald does not run them.

connection.description: Removed by ADR 0037 with spec.connections. An organization connection, by name; the inline form (type) and the connector form (connector) were removed in phase 4 (connection-inline-removed).

connectorConnection.description: Removed: a connection from the connector catalog, which never shipped. Any key not listed here was a setting of the connector.

connector.description: A catalog connector, curated or org-private: name, or name@version.

name.description: Unique in the factory; defaults to the connector's name.

agents.description: Agents that may use the connection; tools may narrow it further.

tools.description: Overrides of the catalog's per-tool defaults, by served tool name (<connection>__<tool>).

enabled.description: false: the tool is never served.

agents.description: A subset of the connection's agents.

access.description: The catalog's class for the tool; accepted, never required.

image.description: stdio: the MCP server's container image, run by goald as a hardened sidecar for each run that uses the connection. Pin it: a version tag (not latest) or a digest (name:1.2.3@sha256:...). Validation warns about an unpinned image and the gateway does not start one.

command.description: stdio: arguments that replace the image's command (its entrypoint is kept). Words that are secret references (env:NAME) are resolved on the host.

env.description: stdio: the sidecar's environment. References are resolved on the host and reach only the sidecar, never the agent's container.

network.description: stdio: give the sidecar outbound network access (Docker's default bridge; host.docker.internal is the host). Without it the sidecar has no network at all, which suits servers that only work on their stdio. Servers that browse, call APIs or reach a database need it.

source.description: A local folder (./skills/x) or a skills.sh reference (skills.sh:owner/repo@skill), pinned by the lockfile.

origin.description: Where a vendored skill came from: the skills.sh skill and the commit it was copied at. The source stays the local folder (./skills/<name>) it was copied into. Written by the builder; read-only in the UI.

source.description: The rule's markdown file inside the definition, under rules/ (./rules/secrets.md).

environment.description: The environment file the agent's box gets, environments/<name>.yaml; default when omitted.

connections.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): set environment. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

tools.description: Custom rules in Claude Code's permission syntax. builtins replaces them; an agent has one or the other.

code.description: Whether the agent may push, open pull requests and merge (write) or only read the code. Default write when the factory has an entry that writes, read otherwise.

builtins.description: Built-in tools by group, each off, ask or allowed; an omitted group is off. ask is served as off until tool approvals cover built-in tools.

run.description: Bash: a mode, or a mode and the commands it may run (Bash(<command>:*) each).

url.description: One repository (https://github.com/acme/app) or an owner's every repository (https://github.com/acme/*), on a code host the organization lists. No credentials in the URL.

token.description: The {{secret}} that opens the repositories. Required for write; omit it for a public repository that is read.

access.description: write lets agents whose code is write push, open pull requests and merge; read never does.

default.description: The entry an item uses when it names no repository. At most one entry has it, and it must name one repository. The only entry is the default when it names one repository.

routeEntry.description: The agent for a lane, or { agent, agents } to keep agents of the station's slots for the lane.

agents.description: Slots of the station kept for this lane; the lane uses no others.

trigger.description: One intake trigger: when an event arrives (on, filter) and its checks pass (only), create an item (create) within the limits (ADR 0026).

name.description: Names the trigger in the API, the UI and the firing log; unique within the factory.

on.description: What the trigger fires on: schedule; <sender>.<event> (github.check_run), that event from every webhook of the sender open to the factory; <webhook>.<event>, that event to one organization webhook; or <webhook>, every event to it. github.check_run.failed and github.issues.labeled, as written before, read as github.check_run with conclusion failure and github.issues with action labeled, and webhook.<name>[.<event>] as <name>[.<event>].

cron.description: When on is schedule, and only then: five cron fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week).

timeZone.description: When on is schedule, and only then: the IANA time zone the cron is read in. Defaults to UTC.

filter.description: Filters on the event's normalized fields, which the sender's event table gives, and on its payload; every one given must match. Publish refuses a filter on a field the event never supplies.

repo.description: The event's repository, owner/name in any case, is this one or one of this list; leaving it out watches every repository.

action.description: The event's action (opened, labeled, completed…) is this one or one of this list.

conclusion.description: The event's conclusion (failure, success…) is this one or one of this list.

paths.description: Globs; the event matches when any changed path matches one.

authors.description: The event's sender is one of these.

skipBots.description: Drop events whose sender is a bot.

match.description: Payload fields by dot path (check_run.app.slug), each matched against a value or a list of values; all must match.

only.description: Checks made before an item is created, in this order.

failuresInARow.description: Passes when the same check failed on the last n events for it.

dedupe.description: An event field, dotted (check.name); passes when no open item this trigger created holds the same value of it.

modelAgrees.description: Ignored (ADR 0040): the model check is removed. A trigger that has it skips every event that reaches it, and the definition loads with the warning field-ignored: turn the trigger into a check.

question.description: The yes or no question the model answered. Ignored.

key.description: The {{secret}} that paid for the check. Ignored.

connection.description: Removed by ADR 0037 (moved-to-environment): set key. Accepted so versions published before still load and run until Goal converts them.

station.description: The station id the item starts at.

lane.description: The item's lane: a key of that station's route.

expedite.description: Put the item in the expedite flow.

title.description: The item's title; {{field}} placeholders take the event's normalized fields, and {{payload.<path>}} any field of its body, each quoted, on one line and at most 200 characters. The title is cut to 300 characters.

brief.description: The item's brief, or the path of a Markdown file in the definition that holds it (./triggers/<name>.md), as an agent's prompt is; {{field}} and {{payload.<path>}} placeholders take the event's values, which reach agents only as untrusted data.

repositories.description: The item's repositories, each matched against runtime.repositories, owner patterns included and in any case: an entry's name, host/owner/name, an https URL, or a template such as {{repo}} (owner/name, on the host of the entry that covers it). A value that renders empty adds none; an item that names none gets the default entry. An event whose value no entry matches is skipped at Create.

trusted.description: File the item a delivery makes as trusted, so a person need not merge its work. Refused for the gitlab and token senders, and on a GitHub webhook unless filter.authors is set.

limits.description: Caps on what the trigger creates.

perDay.description: At most this many items created by the trigger since the start of the UTC day.

perHour.description: At most this many items created by the trigger in the hour before an event. Defaults to 10 for an event trigger; a schedule has none.

perCheck.description: Only with check: at most this many items one check files; what is over it is skipped, "over the limit". Defaults to 5. A check's perDay counts the items the trigger filed, not its firings.

pauseOnBudget.description: Skip events while the factory's budget is spent (today the weekly budget).

check.description: When on is schedule, and only then: each firing runs an agent that looks at the source and answers what to file, instead of filing an item (ADR 0040). The cron may fire at most every 5 minutes, and one check per trigger runs at a time. Publish warns when the agent may use tools that aren't read-only; a check never edits or runs commands, and clones nothing.

agent.description: An agent of the factory; the check runs with its environment, tools and model.

brief.description: What to look for and what is worth an item, or the path of a Markdown file in the definition that holds it (./triggers/<name>.md).

maxUsd.description: The most one check may spend.

timeout.description: How long one check may run, such as 5m; at most 1h.

triggerValues.description: One value, or a list of values one of which must match.

name.description: Display name; id stays the key everything references.

description.description: The note shown under the station.

route.description: Pick the agent by the item's lane instead of one fixed agent, e.g. { backend: backend-engineer, frontend: frontend-engineer }. An entry is an agent name or { agent, agents }: an entry with agents: n gets n of the station's slots kept for its lane, and that lane uses no others; entries without a count share the station's remaining slots. The counts add up to at most the station's agents.

agents.description: Parallel agent containers at this station.

wip.description: Max items in progress at this station.

buffer.description: Items kept ready in front of the station (use at the constraint).

output.description: Name of a contract the station's result must satisfy.

checks.description: Checks the station's output must pass before the item moves on. A command check runs in the run's workspace with CI=true and GOAL_BASE_BRANCH, the branch the item's pull request goes into; GOAL_BASE_BRANCH is empty when that is the repository's default branch.

items.description: A check, or its shorthand: "schema", "evidence-links" or a command line ("go test ./...").

action.description: On a human station or an agent station with a gate: what goald does when the human or the gate approves. merge merges every pull request the item's outputs name first (the pull_request and pull_requests fields of each station's latest output, the gate's own included), each through the factory's code host connection for its host; at a gate goald merges as the engine, and a refused merge blocks the item at the gate.

merges.description: Only on a station with action merge: how many items it integrates into the same merge target at once. A merge target is the branch an item's pull request merges into: the default branch for a standalone item or an assembly's landing, and the assembly's integration branch for a part. serialize (the default): one item per merge target at a time; allow: several at once.

waitFor.description: Make goald wait for CI on the item's pushed commits (ADR 0044): a run at the station starts only once CI on the item's current commits has finished, and after a run pushes, the item moves on only once CI on what it pushed has passed. ci uses the defaults; { ci: { grace, max, rounds } } sets any of them, a field left out taking its default. Nothing here names a host, a CI system, a workflow or a check: goald reads every check the code host reports for the commit.

oneOf.description: Wait for CI with the defaults: grace 5m, max 60m, rounds 3.

ci.description: Wait for CI, with any of the defaults changed. max must be above grace.

grace.description: How long after the run ended a first check may take to appear, such as 5m; a commit with no check by then gets no CI, and the wait ends.

max.description: The longest goald waits for CI on one commit, such as 60m; CI not finished by then counts as failed, and the station runs again.

rounds.description: How many CI rounds one visit to the station gets; after that many, the item blocks for a person, naming the failing checks.

context.description: What goald preloads into the feedback of every run at this station. inflight: an In flight section listing up to 30 of the factory's open items and assemblies with the paths each expects to change, ranked by overlap with the item.

triggers.description: Rules that turn an event, a schedule or a webhook delivery into a work item (ADR 0026). Each name is unique within the factory.

intake.description: Ignored: board.triggers replaces it (ADR 0026, ADR 0040). Still accepted so existing definitions load, with the warning field-ignored.

targets.description: What the line aims for; flow metrics show each against its target. Omit a target to have none.

leadTimeHours.description: p85 lead time, created to done, in hours.

expediteLeadTimeMinutes.description: Lead time of each expedite item, in minutes.

assemblies.description: How runs keep item branches fresh, what a merge conflict does, whether items that edit the same files are built together whether a station's plan becomes an assembly, whether later runs hear what changed since a plan and whether an assembly's parts merge into an integration branch. Omitted keys take their defaults.

freshBase.description: How a run brings an existing item branch up to date with the default branch; default rebase.

onConflict.description: What a merge conflict does: send the item back as rework (default) or leave it to a person.

overlap.description: serialize (the default): an item whose files overlap those of an item in flight waits for it; allow: build them in parallel.

materialize.description: true (the default): a station whose output has a non-empty plan ([{key, title, lane, brief, paths, needs}]) makes the item an assembly, its parts queued at that station; false: the plan is ignored and the item moves on.

changedSince.description: true: a station with context [inflight] that finishes an item records the default branch's head of each of the item's repositories as that repository's base commit (a plan's parts inherit them), and every later run of the item gets a Changed since your plan section per repository listing the commits since then that changed files its paths match. false (the default): nothing is recorded.

integration.description: Whether an assembly's parts merge into one integration branch, goal/a<root number>-<root title slug>, that lands on the default branch at a gate (ADR 0033). Omitted keys take their defaults.

mode.description: trunk (the default): each part merges into the default branch. branch: an assembly's parts merge into its integration branch, which lands at the landing station; the line needs a station with action merge.

refresh.description: When the integration branch takes in the default branch: onLand (the default), when it lands, or eachPart, before each part runs.

minParts.description: The fewest parts an assembly needs for an integration branch; one with fewer stays on trunk. Default 0.

landAt.description: The station where the integration branch lands: an agent station with a gate and action merge. Default: the first station with action merge after the station whose plan made the assembly.

dependencies.description: Which station output fields set an item's dependencies. The platform names no field; an omitted key maps none.

paths.description: The top-level output field whose list of file globs replaces the item's paths when a station finishes with a non-empty one. An entry may start with owner/name: to name its repository (acme/web:src/**); an entry without one is in the item's first repository. Items whose paths overlap, in the same repository, wait for each other under assemblies.overlap serialize: the same path in two repositories does not overlap.

after.description: The output property listing the open items of this factory, outside the output's plan, that the work must follow, as item refs <factory>#<number>. Each becomes a linked edge from the item, or from every part of its plan with no in-plan needs; a ref that is malformed, of another factory, unknown, done, cancelled or would close a cycle fails the output.

outputs.description: Which station output fields goald reads besides the contract's own. The platform names no field; an omitted key maps none.

followUps.description: The top-level output field that holds follow-ups: work an agent noticed outside its item. goald keeps the first 10 entries of each accepted output on the item, each text once. An entry is a string (text for triage) or an object with text and optionally for, an open item <factory>#<number> to note, or start, {at, in, after} with a title and optionally type, lane, repositories and factory, an item of its own filed when the work lands; start wins over for. A station contract that declares the field must declare it as a plain array: no $ref, no maxItems and no required on its items.

close.description: The top-level output field whose text closes the item: when an accepted output gives 10 to 500 characters there, goald cancels the item at its station with that text as the reason, the agent the actor. Only an item a trigger or a follow-up filed, and never a part, can be closed. On a person's item, a part, an output that also plans parts, or a text outside the limits, the output fails its check and the agent asks a person instead. Empty or only whitespace closes nothing.

repositories.description: The top-level output field whose list of repositories joins the item, recorded as joined output. Each entry is a runtime.repositories entry's name, owner/name or an https URL an entry covers, resolved as at filing. An item keeps at most 10 repositories: when the names would give it more, or one is not a repository of the factory, the output fails its check with the reason and the agent tries again. Repositories join only with an accepted output, never with a gate's rejection.

followUpsFrom.description: The factories, by metadata.id, this factory accepts follow-ups from: their notes and their items. None by default.

retry.description: How often a claim runs an item again after a failure that is not the item's fault. Omitted keys take their defaults.

transient.description: Runs whose sandbox was lost to its infrastructure (a redeploy, a box restart, a network blip) or whose prepare failed before the agent started (goal-agent prepare exited non-zero, such as a tool download that timed out): each runs again in a new box after a backoff that doubles with each loss.

attempts.description: The most runs one claim makes when its sandbox is lost or its prepare fails, both counted together; the failure that reaches it blocks the item. Default 3.

librarian.description: Ignored (ADR 0039): Jonah proposes knowledge from the line. A definition that has it loads with the warning field-ignored.

after.description: Stations whose completion triggers the librarian.

kaizen.description: Ignored (ADR 0039): Jonah reviews the line once a day. A definition that has it loads with the warning field-ignored.

jonah.description: Jonah, which reviews the line once a day and proposes changes to the definition (ADR 0039).

enabled.description: Whether Jonah reviews this factory at all.

proposeAfter.description: The items with the same cause an observation needs before it becomes a proposal.

share.description: Jonah's budget, as a percent of what the line spent in the last 7 days, from 0% to 100%. Each review may spend a fifth of it, and Jonah's spend never triggers runtime.budget.onExhausted.

weeklyUsd.description: Ignored (ADR 0039): Jonah's budget is share. A definition that has it loads with the warning field-ignored.

model.description: The review run's model; runtime.model when omitted.
